title: V.J. Edgecombe goes third to 76ers, highest a Baylor player has ever been picked in NBA draft - NewsBreak
text: V.J. Edgecombe is heading to the Philadelphia 76ers, getting picked third overall in Wednesday’s NBA draft. The 6-foot-4 guard, who averaged 15 points per game as a freshman in his lone season at Baylor, is the first Bears player to ever go in the Top 5 of the NBA draft. \ "I don't have words either, man," Edgecombe said on ESPN shortly after being drafted. "I'm blessed. To be the third pick? It's a dream come true. I spent countless years just sitting there watching the NBA draft." Ekpe Udoah, who went No. 6 to the Golden State Warriors in 2010, was the previously highest-drafted player in Baylor’s history. The Bears have been on a serious run under Scott Drew, who led Baylor to the national title in 2021. Baylor has had nine first-round picks during Drew’s time in Waco. Before that, only three Bears — Vinnie Johnson, Terry Teagle and Brian Skinner — had ever gone in the first round. The top two of the draft was set way before draft day with everyone knowing Duke's Cooper Flagg was headed to Dallas with the No. 1 pick, followed by Rutgers' Dylan Harper going to San Antonio at No. 2. There was plenty of question about who would go third, but Philadelphia made Edgcombe its choice, setting off a wave of tears from the Edgecombe family at Barclays Center. "We came from nothing," Edgecombe said shortly after being picked. "We are truly blessed just to be in this position. I know the emotions are high right now." Edgecombe, who grew up in the Bahamas before moving to the United States in the ninth grade, got high marks in the pre-draft process for his competitiveness and high character. Of course, there’s also Edgecombe’s athleticism, possessing elevation that resulted in highlight dunks throughout his lone year in college. Edgecombe, who turns 20 in July, shot a respectable 34% from the 3-point line at Baylor, but his smooth stroke leads scouts to believe that will improve as he matures. He also shined in the 2025 FIBA Olympic Qualifying Tournament, standing out on a Bahamian team that included NBA players Buddy Hield, Deandre Ayton and Eric Gordon. Edgecombe could be part of an immediate playoff team. The 76ers’ streak of seven straight postseason appearances was snapped last season after being hit by injuries. With Joel Embiid expected to return and paired with high-scoring guard Tyrese Maxey, Philadelphia could contend in a week Eastern Conference.
